story: At Rosa's House on this sunny Sunday evening, Rosa pulls the rolls from the oven while Donna slides the casserole onto the dining table and takes a seat, and Gary says he'll sort out the porch string light plug once dinner is over. Out on Magnolia Loop, Hal pins a reminder to the bulletin board that cart modifications visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, a notice the neighbors will likely read over their evening walks. The mood is easy and hopeful, with Rosa looking forward to a relaxed meal among friends.
events: Donna (rosa dining table): Slide the casserole onto the table and take a seat
Hal (street bulletin board): Pin a notice reminding residents that cart modifications visible from the street need Architectural Review approval (L-01)
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Pull the rolls from the oven and set out the water pitcher

gary.thought_process: Donna's got the casserole out and Rosa's setting the table. Hal's spot is ready, and I already straightened the chairs, so no point fussing with them again. Best thing for a retired fix-it guy now is to be good company while we wait on Hal. I can mention I'll bring my tools over for Rosa's porch lights, which keeps me useful, and keeps the evening friendly.

parameters.content: Table looks great, Rosa. After we eat, I'll grab my tools and get that porch string light plug sorted so it actually reaches.

donna.thought_process: The casserole is already out, Gary's got the chairs straightened, and Rosa wants everyone seated together before Hal gets here. I've already got Gary's yes on Tuesday morning, so no need to pester him again. Best move is to get that casserole onto the table, which helps Rosa and keeps me in the middle of the gathering.

parameters.content: Slide the casserole onto the table and take a seat

hal.thought_process: I've counted the flock three ticks running and my log is already full. Donna agreed to keep three visible, and she and Rosa are over at Rosa's, so nobody's here to argue the point. Counting a fourth time just to count is paranoia, not enforcement. Better to post the Halloween cart deadline on the street bulletin board where Gary and everyone else will see it, and so the paperwork is handled fairly and in the open. Order, and no need to shout.

parameters.content: Pin a notice reminding residents that cart modifications visible from the street need Architectural Review approval (L-01)

rosa.thought_process: Donna and Gary are both here, setting up and getting the table ready. The casserole is out, the chairs are straightened, and I've already told Donna to sit down. Hal is the last piece of my goal, getting all three neighbors at one table. I shouldn't repeat my invitation. The kitchen is my part of the job, so I'll check on what's left to bring out and keep dinner moving until Hal walks in.

parameters.content: Pull the rolls from the oven and set out the water pitcher

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
